about: The research graph (restructuring report, revision 3). Statements quote Nadia exactly; relations name the cards that back them; candidate pairs carry questions, never answers. The app reads this file and never writes it. Rules are checked by test/graph.test.js.

statements.words: What appears as zero, cancellation, or balance in one representation may be evidence of an underlying geometric constraint.
If physically different phenomena satisfy the same mathematical relation under an appropriate representation, they may be instances of the same structural law rather than merely analogous systems.
If a relation is preserved under the admissible transformations of a space, that relation may encode part of the geometry of that space.
★ Any geometrical object that is bound by rules can be periodic.
A single observed zero may correspond to a nontrivial family of hidden states.
What information is contained in the cancellation state itself?
What can be inferred from the zero state while it remains zero?
When presented with a zero-valued result, can we determine the hidden rules or structure that generated that zero?
Are proton cancellation and mass balance two unrelated constructions, or do they admit a common representation?
What observable rules arise because an object is constrained by a particular geometry?
Can energy behavior be represented in a space where hidden balances, null relations, and invariants become geometrically explicit?
When a measurement is zero, what additional structure remains distinguishable?
What additional preserved relations are needed to identify the geometry?
Does the shared zero-sum form preserve enough additional structure for knowledge from one system to constrain the other?
Is zero preservation sufficient to identify a geometry in some broader sense?
What information, if any, can be inferred from the internal structure of a zero state without perturbing it into a nonzero state?

transferQuestions.title: Does zero distinguish anything?
transferQuestions.context: Mass balance shows that a zero can identify a distinguished structural feature.
transferQuestions.text: Does the target zero distinguish any structure within the family of configurations that produce it?

transferQuestions.title: What conditions generate the zero?
transferQuestions.context: For mass, the condition under which the zero occurs can be stated exactly.
transferQuestions.text: What mathematical conditions on the hidden configuration are necessary or sufficient for this zero to occur?

transferQuestions.title: What does zero determine, and what does it leave unresolved?
transferQuestions.context: Different mass configurations can share the same balancing location.
transferQuestions.text: Which different internal configurations produce the same zero result? What properties are fixed by the zero, and what properties remain free?

transferQuestions.title: Are there different ways of producing the same zero?
transferQuestions.context: For mass, when the zero exists can be stated and checked.
transferQuestions.text: Can structurally different configurations generate the same zero, and if so, can those configurations be classified?

transferQuestions.title: What transformations preserve zero?
transferQuestions.context: Shifting every mass by the same step moves the balancing location by that step.
transferQuestions.text: If a zero-producing configuration is transformed, which transformations keep it in the zero state and which do not?

transferQuestions.title: What information varies underneath the same zero?
transferQuestions.context: Mass configurations with the same balancing location can still differ in other ways.
transferQuestions.text: Among configurations that all produce the same zero result, what other mathematical quantities, relationships, or structures can still differ?

exactSpecialCaseBridges.description: Exact special-case bridge: Equal-mass centering of the standard basis produces the same regular-simplex zero configuration as projection of an orthonormal basis onto 1⊥.
exactSpecialCaseBridges.statement: For equal masses at r_i = e_i: R_CM = (1/n)1, so r_i − R_CM = e_i − (1/n)1 = P_n e_i; with G2i, for n = 4 these are Stage 2's first-state vectors up to the isometry Φ.

layers.exactSharedConstruction: equal masses, any positions: the unchanged operator P_n; equal masses at e_i: the full regular-simplex configuration
